headline: Approved FY27 goals covering the library capital campaign, barriers to the temporary location, and community outreach.
summary: The committee heard library updates on programming, statistics, and the O’Brien Community Center capital campaign. It also approved its FY27 goals and planned a presentation to the Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission.

10/1/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Lauren Read, Dana Visser, Prudence Doherty, Jess Wignall, Colleen 
McCormick Moore
City Staff Present: Nate Eddy
Guests Present: n/a
Call to Order by: Motion - Jess, Second - Colleen
Meeting Start Time: 6:39 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Lauren Read
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Nate
Second: Prudence
Decision: Approved
Public Comment
N/A
Committee Member Updates
Jess reported that she attended Pride event, CHT was not doing any fundraising at event.
Library Updates
September Library Updates
Programming:
From September 3 - 18, we hosted the 1619: Arrival of the First Africans Traveling Exhibit on 
loan from the Hampton History Museum. The window display was viewed by 40 students on a 
class visit from WHS, in addition to passive interactions from pedestrians.
Drop-in Mahjong play for adults has started on Fridays from 10 AM – 12 PM.
l Janice, local community member wanted to facilitate  
l About 5-6 people attending regularly
On September 5, we partnered with the Lake Champlain Basin Program to host a watershed 
model program for youth.
Kirsten has restarted the Community Helper Storytime and on September 11, we hosted Dr. 
O’Bryan from the Winooski Community Health Center. Up next is a postal worker from Winooski 
USPS. 
STEAM, weekly storytime and playgroups, and after school programming for youth all continue.
Starting in October, we’ll be offering a monthly song and storytime in Spanish by Argentinian 
performer Constancia Gomez.
Statistics:
Although physical circulation was slightly down from July, card registrations and door count 
were both higher from the previous month.
o Circulation: 1241 (September) vs. 1263 (August)
o Door count: 963 (September) vs. 1077 (August)
o E-circ: 984 (September) vs. 1025 (August)
o 61 new library card registrations vs. 43 (August)
Friends of the Winooski Library: 
The Friends held a fall book drive at the library on Saturday, September 26, and received a nice 
haul of donations!
Building Updates
On Tuesday, Nate and Elaine attended the CHT funding meeting. To date, $2.65M has been 
raised toward the entire OCC project, ~53% of what’s needed. The group brainstormed some 
other strategies and agreed to shift into a more publicly facing fundraising campaign and 
communicate out to the community about the project. The plan is to share a new one-page doc 
with QR code for people to donate, then in the new year the Library will hold another Open 
House to raise more community interest. Looking for more buy-in from the Community Health 
Center group, hoping new CEO will be able to help.
General:
The Vermont Library Association is proposing to use some of the Meta settlement funds 
awarded to the state (~$90M over 10 years) for a Youth and Teen Library Spaces Grant 
Program, administered through the Vermont Department of Libraries, that could help libraries 
renovate and create welcoming, flexible spaces for young people that foster connections & 
creativity. Capital improvement needs remain significant for libraries across Vermont, and 
pursuing targeted funding opportunities like this is an important part of VLA’s broader strategy to 
address those needs. VLA has engaged with legislative allies and sent their request to the 
Governor, asking him to include libraries as his administration considers how the settlement 
funds should be used and drafts their proposed FY28 Budget.
The South Burlington Library has recently migrated its ILS to KOHA and joins a number of other 
libraries – including us – in a shared cataloging system. This allows member libraries to verify 
HomeCard standing among patrons as well as view member library holdings.
We have submitted an application to CLiF for their Early Childhood Literacy grant which if 
awarded includes new books, literacy kits, funds for family engagement activities, and $500 in 
flex funds to support literacy-related programming.
October 19th is Vermont Library Day.
Discuss and Approve FY27 Committee Goals
Library Committee FY27 Goals
1. Remain informed of the Library and O’Brien Community Center Capital Campaign effort 
and work to promote awareness within the Winooski community.  
2. Identify and implement methods to collect information about barriers to accessing the 
temporary library location from the west side of the city.  
3. Perform outreach at a minimum of three community events to raise the profile of the 
library and its services. 
Discussion around goals - making sure we all know what O’Brien Community Center Capital 
Campaign, action items around events.
Lauren will reach out to Sarah about Holiday Market - first outreach event
Should we reach out/join Friends for October Farmers Market
Should we bring goal No. 2 to Safe, Healthy, Connected People commission to begin gathering 
information - committee agreed its a good idea and will bring it to the meeting
How do we accomplish No. 2? QR codes for some locations, Front Porch Forum post with 
form, school events
l First step - next meeting discuss the questions we want to ask for form
Also keep barriers to access
Motion by: Jess
Second: Lauren
Decision: Approved
Planning for Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission
Tuesday, October 13 at 5:30 p.m. - Library
Dana can attend, Lauren is a maybe, Jess/Colleen cannot attend
Nate may request to move the meeting to October 20 because quite a few board members can't 
attend
Agenda
l Nate will make a brief PowerPoint presentation about the library 
l Question and answer session  
l Library Committee is introduced; Prudence gives some information about Committee; 
discuss FY26 accomplishments and FY27 goals  
¡ Mention CHT funding, Comprehensive plan feedback 
¡ If one-pager is ready, we can present
l Ask some questions of the SHCP committee members
Nate to email out proposed presentation - members to send feedback to Nate
Other Business
No other business.
Adjourn
Motion by: Prudence
Second:  Colleen 
Meeting End Time: 7:14 pm
I.

VI.
VII.
VIII.
IX.
